question: Why is the 'Action items' section described as the most important part of a post-mortem?
options: Action items are required by most compliance frameworks
A post-mortem without action items is just a story — action items with owners and due dates turn the incident into a prevention plan that reduces future incidents
Action items help determine who was at fault for the incident
The action items section is the shortest and easiest to review
explanation: The purpose of a post-mortem is not to assign blame but to learn and prevent recurrence. Without concrete action items (with owners and due dates tracked in an issue tracker), the same incident will happen again. Action items transform an incident report into an improvement roadmap.

question: Why should voice AI systems configure fallback providers for each component (STT, LLM, TTS)?
options: Fallback providers reduce costs through load balancing
Every external provider will eventually have outages — a slower backup TTS voice or alternative LLM is better than complete silence or failure for callers
Using multiple providers improves audio quality through averaging
Fallback providers are required by LiveKit's terms of service
explanation: Provider outages are inevitable. If your sole TTS provider goes down and you have no fallback, every caller gets silence. A slower backup voice or alternative model provides degraded but functional service. Treating provider outages as inevitable rather than exceptional drives you to build resilience into the architecture.

question: What does the '3 AM test' for operational processes evaluate?
options: Whether an engineer woken by a page can follow the runbook, diagnose the issue, and resolve it without needing to message anyone else
Whether the on-call rotation has 24/7 coverage across time zones
Whether automated systems can self-heal overnight without human intervention
Whether the system can handle traffic at 3 AM when usage is lowest
explanation: The 3 AM test is a practical litmus test for runbook quality. If a groggy engineer cannot follow the documented steps to resolution independently, the runbook needs more detail — exact commands, common causes, escalation paths. Every additional person they need to wake up increases mean time to resolution.
